title: Adoption Signal Atlas: Prioritized Indicators for Emerging Model Fit
creator: Leah Kim
description: Create a repeatable, prioritized atlas of adoption signals that product, GTM, and partner teams can use to detect enterprise readiness of emerging open and vendor models. This ticket covers hypothesis definition, signal sourcing, scoring rubric, an initial 30-model pilot, and a lightweight dashboard for weekly monitoring. Output should enable fast go/no-go decisions on onboarding a model into Redwood API, Dedicated, or Private offerings.
objectives: Define 12 orthogonal adoption signals (technical, commercial, regulatory, ecosystem)
Operationalize signal collection for weekly refreshes (APIs, scraping, partner reports)
Build a scoring rubric to convert signals into a 0-100 model readiness score
Pilot the atlas on 30 candidate models across hardware/quantization compatibility buckets
Produce a handoff package for Runtime and Sales with recommended playbooks per readiness tier
deliverables: Signal taxonomy doc (Confluence) with definitions and data sources
Signal ingestion spreadsheet and ETL instructions (CSV + runbook)
Scoring rubric and threshold mapping to readiness tiers (0-100 -> Not Ready / Observability / Production-Ready)
Pilot report: 30-model matrix with recommended deployment paths and risk notes
Lightweight tableau/Looker dashboard mock and weekly monitoring query set
success_metrics: Signal coverage >= 90% for the 30 pilot models
Pilot rubric precision: >80% agreement with SME manual tags for Production-Ready vs Not Ready
Time to identify a fallback model for a critical customer use case reduced from 2 days to <6 hours
>1 internal product or sales decision in quarter driven by atlas output
data_sources: Model release notes and GitHub repos
Open-source community activity (stars, forks, contributors) via GH API
Vendor announcements and license terms (web scraping + partner feeds)
Cloud availability matrix (region, instance types) from infra partners
risks: Signal noise: community metrics can be gamed or lag reality
Data access: some vendor/security signals require partner approvals
False positives: readiness score may miss subtle integration blockers (quant-kernel mismatches)
Maintenance burden: weekly refresh may require engineering support beyond initial scope
acceptance_criteria: Confluence taxonomy published with at least 12 signals and example model annotations
Automated ingest for 5 of the highest-value signals (benchmarks, GH activity, license check) documented
Pilot sheet populated for 30 models with computed readiness scores and qualitative notes
Handoff deck and operational runbook delivered to Runtime and Sales
